paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is a form of oral-facial-digital syndrome. Its oral, facial and digital malformations occur together with acromelic short stature and genu valgum, and some of its features overlap with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (Phadke et al., 1999). Thevenon et al. (2016) classified it as an unclassified OFDS with skeletal dysplasia, marked by short stature, brachymesophalangia and stocky femoral necks, without rib shortening or thoracic narrowing.

paragraphs.text: Phadke et al. (1999) reported a consanguineous family with what they described as a new variety of oral-facial-digital syndrome (OFDS). The affected members had oral, facial and digital malformations together with acromelic short stature and genu valgum, features that overlap with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome. One of the sibs had urinary incontinence and growth hormone deficiency. The authors noted that neither finding had been reported before in any type of OFDS.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) restudied the consanguineous Indian family first reported by Phadke et al. (1999), in which 3 sibs were affected. Subject II-1, a male, was examined at 25 years of age. He had normal intelligence. His final height was 155 cm (-3 SD), his weight 45 kg (less than -3 SD) and his occipitofrontal circumference 50 cm (mean). His facial features included a square face, short forehead, upslanting palpebral fissures, high nasal bridge, short philtrum and medial clefting of the upper lip. His oral anomalies were supernumerary frenulae and missing incisors. His digital anomalies were pronounced brachydactyly, upper-limb postaxial polydactyly and severe mesophalangeal shortening, and his feet showed preaxial polydactyly with first metatarsal duplication and a gap between the first and second toes. Bone studies showed bilateral short femoral necks with varus femurs and symmetric genu valgum. He had no thoracic deformity and no vertebral anomalies. Heart, renal and abdominal ultrasound examinations were normal.

paragraphs.text: Subject II-2, a female, was examined at 22 years of age (Thevenon et al., 2016). She had normal intelligence and was married with no children. Her final height was 122 cm (-5 SD), her weight 37 kg (-2 SD) and her occipitofrontal circumference 51 cm (mean). Her facial features included a square face, narrow forehead, enophthalmia, upslanting palpebral fissures, broad nasal bridge, bilateral hypopigmented pseudoclefts and medial labial clefting. She had missing incisors and supernumerary frenulae. Her digital anomalies were marked brachydactyly, four-limb postaxial polydactyly that was surgically removed in infancy, mesophalangeal shortening and bifid terminal phalanges. Her feet showed first metatarsal duplication and absent intermediate phalanges of the toes. Skeletal studies showed vertebral bodies with medial notches but no platyspondyly, bilateral cervical ribs without a narrow thorax, gracile long bones and shortened femoral necks. Puberty was not delayed, and brain MRI was normal. The third sib, subject II-3, died at 17 years of age of a complicated pulmonary infection.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) studied the consanguineous Indian family first reported by Phadke et al. (1999). In the region of homozygosity on chromosome 3, they identified a homozygous synonymous c.777G-A transition (lys259-to-lys; K259K) in the IFT57 gene, which affects the last base of exon 6. Sanger sequencing confirmed that all 3 affected sibs were homozygous for the variant. The variant was not present in the ExAC database or in 50 northern Indian controls. In patient fibroblasts, the variant produced a complex splicing pattern: the normal transcript was present, along with 3 aberrant transcripts lacking exon 6, exons 5-6 or exons 4-6, which could be detected only after inhibition of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. IFT57 mRNA levels were also reduced. The authors considered the mutation hypomorphic.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) found that primary cilia were normal in number and length in fibroblasts from patients with the IFT57 mutation. However, IFT57 staining at the ciliary tip was reduced (35% of cilia, compared with 90% in controls) and basal body staining was increased, indicating defective anterograde ciliary transport. Stimulation with SAG induced GLI1 only poorly in patient fibroblasts, and siRNA knockdown of IFT57 in control fibroblasts abolished GLI1 induction. These results indicated impaired sonic hedgehog (SHH) signaling.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) studied 3 affected sibs from a consanguineous Indian family with OFD18, first reported by Phadke et al. (1999). All 3 were homozygous for a c.777G-A transition in the IFT57 gene, a synonymous change (lys259-to-lys; K259K) at the last base of exon 6, and Sanger sequencing confirmed the homozygous variant in each of them. The variant was not present in ExAC or in 50 northern Indian controls. In patient fibroblasts, the variant produced normal transcript plus 3 aberrant transcripts that skipped exon 6, exons 5-6 or exons 4-6. The aberrant transcripts could be detected only after inhibition of nonsense-mediated decay, and IFT57 mRNA levels were reduced. Patient fibroblasts showed reduced IFT57 at the ciliary tip and poor GLI1 induction after SAG stimulation.

checks.claim: All 3 affected sibs of the Indian OFD18 family were homozygous for a c.777G-A transition in the IFT57 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the variation at a homozygous status in the 3 affected subjects.

checks.claim: The IFT57 c.777G-A variant is a synonymous change (K259K) at the last base of exon 6.
checks.evidence_quote: The synonymous c.777G>A substitution in exon 6 affects IFT57 pre-mRNA splicing
checks.explanation: Paper also states the substitution affects the last base of exon 6 and is p.Lys259Lys.

checks.claim: Sanger sequencing confirmed the homozygous IFT57 c.777G-A variant in each of the 3 affected sibs.
checks.evidence_quote: Sanger sequencing confirmed the variation at a homozygous status in the 3 affected subjects.

checks.claim: The IFT57 c.777G-A variant was not present in ExAC.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant was absent from the ExAC database

checks.claim: The IFT57 c.777G-A variant was not present in 50 northern Indian controls.
checks.evidence_quote: absence of the rare variants was verified in 50 healthy subjects from northern India

checks.claim: In patient fibroblasts, the IFT57 c.777G-A variant produced normal transcript plus 3 aberrant transcripts skipping exon 6, exons 5-6 or exons 4-6.
checks.evidence_quote: B) In frame exon 6 skipping. C) In frame skipping of exons 5 and 6. D) Out of frame skipping of exons 4, 5 and 6.
checks.explanation: Normal transcript (A) also present.

checks.claim: The aberrant IFT57 transcripts could be detected only after inhibition of nonsense-mediated decay.
checks.evidence_quote: The pathological transcripts are only detected after inhibition of the NMD pathway.

checks.claim: IFT57 mRNA levels were reduced in fibroblasts with the c.777G-A variant.
checks.evidence_quote: RNA isolated from the subject’s fibroblasts had significantly less IFT57 mRNA than did that of controls (Figure 2D).

checks.claim: Fibroblasts with the IFT57 c.777G-A variant showed reduced IFT57 at the ciliary tip.
checks.evidence_quote: In the subject’s fibroblasts, staining of the ciliary tip with IFT57 was significantly decreased (90% versus 35%; p<0.001)

checks.claim: Fibroblasts with the IFT57 c.777G-A variant showed poor GLI1 induction after SAG stimulation.
checks.evidence_quote: Stimulation of the SHH pathway by Smoothened Agonist (SAG) showed poor induction of Gli1 mRNA expression in fibroblasts from the IFT57-mutated subject compared with control fibroblasts
